title: Get started with balancesample
text: example uses simulated data 300 patients three sites. Age income skewed, diagnosis rare level. outcome depends age, income, diagnosis.
code: library(balancesample)  set.seed(2026) n <- 300 d <- data.frame(   age = rgamma(n, shape = 4, rate = 0.1),   income = rlnorm(n, meanlog = 10, sdlog = 0.6),   diagnosis = factor(sample(     c("none", "mild", "severe"),     n,     replace = TRUE,     prob = c(0.6, 0.3, 0.1)   )),   site = factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), n, replace = TRUE)) ) severe <- d$diagnosis == "severe" d$outcome <- 0.05 * d$age + 0.3 * log(d$income) + 1.5 * severe + rnorm(n)

code: split <- balanced_initial_split(   d,   prop = 0.8,   balance = c(age, income),   exact = c(diagnosis, site) ) train <- rsample::training(split) balance_check(split) #> # Balance check: 1 split, 4 variables #> # |SMD| > 0.1 in 0 of 4 variables, energy distance 0.0291 #>  #> variable   level         SMD #> age                -0.000652 #> income             -9.91e-05 #> diagnosis  mild     0.00927 #> diagnosis  none    -0.00846 #> diagnosis  severe   0 #> site       A       -0.0174 #> site       B        0.0367 #> site       C       -0.0174 #>  #> # tibble::as_tibble() gives all 9 rows. folds <- balanced_vfold_cv(   train,   v = 5,   balance = c(age, income),   exact = c(diagnosis, site) ) library(ggplot2) autoplot(balance_check(folds)) library(balancesample) library(parsnip) library(tune) library(workflows)  wf <- workflow(   outcome ~ age + income + diagnosis + site,   decision_tree(     tree_depth = tune(),     min_n = tune(),     mode = "regression"   ) ) res <- tune_grid(wf, resamples = folds, grid = 6) show_best(res, metric = "rmse", n = 3) #> # A tibble: 3 × 8 #>   tree_depth min_n .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config         #>        <int> <int> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>           #> 1         12     9 rmse    standard    1.14     5  0.0751 pre0_mod5_post0 #> 2          6     2 rmse    standard    1.16     5  0.0837 pre0_mod3_post0 #> 3          9    24 rmse    standard    1.16     5  0.0558 pre0_mod4_post0 final <- finalize_workflow(wf, select_best(res, metric = "rmse")) final_fit <- last_fit(final, split) collect_metrics(final_fit) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   .metric .estimator .estimate .config         #>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>           #> 1 rmse    standard       1.10  pre0_mod0_post0 #> 2 rsq     standard       0.509 pre0_mod0_post0

"twinning" uses data twinning twinning package (Vakayil Joseph, 2022). takes one set data time. takes row nearest unused neighbours small group keeps first row set. next group starts unused row closest last group’s farthest neighbour, set covers data way whole data . within exact stratum. folds, default strategy repeats rows left. needs twinning package, allows split proportions, splits small strata random (folds, strata fewer 2 * v rows). "rerandomize" uses rerandomization (Morgan Rubin, 2012). draws stratified random splits scores one Mahalanobis imbalance: distance means sets takes correlations columns account. folds, score largest imbalance fold rest. keeps first draw scores cutoff, set 100 pilot draws 10% draws pass. none 1,000 draws passes, uses best one, warning. balances means , needs extra package. "interaction" cuts numeric column four bins rank, crosses levels categorical columns, stratifies random result. Within exact stratum, cells fewer 10% rows pooled. Crossed cells get small fast: , age income quartiles 9 exact strata, largest cell 8 rows cutoff 30, every cell pooled folds random within exact strata. baseline shows crossed strata become sparse. compares four full data 10 folds: run, smallest max_abs_smd came anticlust (0.119), smallest mean_abs_smd anticlust (0.037), smallest mean_energy twinning (0.045). come one run method one data set, don’t show method best general, small differences may noise. Start anticlust, watch run time large data. one test one computer, 10 folds four numeric variables, took 0.5 seconds 1,000 rows, 3.7 seconds 3,000 rows, 25 seconds 10,000 rows, 3.6 minutes 30,000 rows. options = list(k_neighbours = 20), row can swap 20 nearest neighbours, runs took 0.3, 1.6, 4.1, 11.7 seconds. code: methods <- c("anticlust", "twinning", "rerandomize", "interaction") by_method <- lapply(methods, function(m) {   f <- balanced_vfold_cv(     d,     v = 10,     balance = c(age, income),     exact = c(diagnosis, site),     method = m   )   s <- summary(balance_check(f))   data.frame(     method = m,     max_abs_smd = max(s$max_abs_smd),     mean_abs_smd = mean(s$mean_abs_smd),     mean_energy = mean(s$energy)   ) }) by_method <- do.call(rbind, by_method) shown <- by_method shown[-1] <- round(shown[-1], 3) shown #>        method max_abs_smd mean_abs_smd mean_energy #> 1   anticlust       0.119        0.037       0.054 #> 2    twinning       0.426        0.099       0.045 #> 3 rerandomize       0.268        0.087       0.055 #> 4 interaction       0.419        0.104       0.066
